title: Jolting Norwegian Grape Leaves Pilaf
description: A tangy, energizing Norwegian dish featuring grape leaves, a unique combination of traditional and ayurvedic elements. To create this shattering pilaf, we will mix crunchy fried rice with a rich blend of spices and herbs, then fill the mixture into grape leaves for a refreshing twist.

ingredients.name: Grape Leaves
ingredients.notes: preferably fresh, or use jarred in brine

ingredients.name: Fenugreek Leaves
ingredients.notes: for a pungent, slightly bitter taste

ingredients.name: Lemon Juice
ingredients.notes: freshly squeezed, for a bright acidity

instructions: Heat 2 tablespoons of ghee in a pan over medium heat, then add 1 cup of fried khao khua rice and stir-fry until lightly toasted.
Add 1 teaspoon of turmeric, 1/2 teaspoon of mustard seeds, and 1 teaspoon of dill weed to the pan, stirring to combine.
Add the grape leaves to the pan, one by one, and fill each leaf with the fried rice mixture, leaving a small border around the edges.
Fold the grape leaves over the filling to enclose, and secure with toothpicks if needed.
In a separate pan, heat 1/2 cup of frying oil over medium heat, then carefully add the stuffed grape leaves and fry until golden brown on all sides.
Remove the grape leaves from the oil and place them on a paper towel-lined plate to drain excess oil.
Serve the Jolting Norwegian Grape Leaves Pilaf hot, garnished with chopped scallions and a squeeze of fresh lemon juice.
